outline: 1942 Permutations involving Grouping, Complements, and Cases

examples.question_text: Eight different students stand in a row for a photograph. Three particular friends must stand together. How many arrangements are possible?
examples.solution_text:
Treat the three friends as one unit. Arrange the six units, then arrange the three friends within their unit.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6!\times3!\\&=720\times6\\&=4320\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Nine different performers appear in a concert. Find the number of possible orders if:

(a) Ava must perform first.

(b) Ava must perform first and Noah must perform last.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Fix Ava first, then arrange the other eight performers.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8!\\&=40320\end{aligned}$

(b) Fix Ava first and Noah last, then arrange the other seven performers.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7!\\&=5040\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Five boys and five girls stand in a row. How many arrangements have boys and girls alternating?
examples.solution_text:
There are two patterns: BGBGBGBGBG and GBGBGBGBGB. Each has $5!$ arrangements of the boys and $5!$ arrangements of the girls.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5!\times5!+5!\times5!\\&=14400+14400\\&=28800\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Four-digit numbers are formed from $\{1,2,3,5,7,8,9\}$ without repetition. How many are:

(a) even?

(b) greater than $7000$?
examples.solution_text:
(a) Fill the last position first: it must contain $2$ or $8$. Fill the other three positions from the six remaining digits.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\times{}^{6}P_{3}\\&=2\times6\times5\times4\\&=240\end{aligned}$

(b) Fill the first position first: it must contain $7$, $8$ or $9$. Fill the other three positions from the six remaining digits.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3\times{}^{6}P_{3}\\&=3\times6\times5\times4\\&=360\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A shelf holds two different Maths books, three different Science books and five different English books. How many arrangements keep the books of each subject together?
examples.solution_text:
Treat each subject as one unit. Arrange the three units, then arrange the books within each unit.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3!\times2!\times3!\times5!\\&=6\times2\times6\times120\\&=8640\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Six boys and three girls sit in a row. How many arrangements have no two girls sitting next to each other?
Seven different students stand in a row. Mia and Leo must not stand next to each other. How many arrangements are possible?
examples.solution_text:
There are $7!$ unrestricted arrangements. If Mia and Leo stand together, treat them as one unit: there are $6!\times2!$ unacceptable arrangements.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7!-6!\times2!\\&=5040-1440\\&=3600\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Four-digit numbers are formed from $\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ without repetition. How many are even and greater than $4000$?
examples.solution_text:
Fill the first and last positions before the middle two. The first digit is $4$, $5$ or $6$; the last digit is even.

Case 1: First digit $4$ or $6$. There are two first-digit choices and three remaining even last-digit choices. Fill the middle positions from the five remaining digits.

$2\times3\times{}^{5}P_{2}=120$

Case 2: First digit $5$. All four even digits are available for the last position. Fill the middle positions from the five remaining digits.

$1\times4\times{}^{5}P_{2}=80$

The cases do not overlap.

$120+80=200$

examples.question_text: Five different students and two different teachers stand in a row. How many arrangements have at least two students between the teachers?
examples.solution_text:
Subtract arrangements with zero or one student between the teachers from all $7!$ arrangements.

Adjacent teachers: treat the teachers as one unit and arrange them internally.

$6!\times2!=1440$

Exactly one student between: choose that student in five ways. Treat the teacher–student–teacher group as one unit, arrange the five units, and order the teachers in two ways.

$5\times5!\times2!=1200$

These unacceptable cases do not overlap.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7!-1440-1200\\&=5040-1440-1200\\&=2400\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored nine worked examples covering the distinct accepted assessment methods. Existing examples: none. Assessments were read only to classify methods; their mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Examples use separate editable prompts and solutions, single-dollar mathematics, phantom gutters where required, and renderer-inherited blue solution prose/math. The gaps diagram uses black marks and 10 pt labels. No files were written; independent example review and actual visual capture remain coordinator stages.

examples.derivation: Three adjacent friends form one unit alongside five other students: six distinct units. Internal friend orders give 6! × 3! = 720 × 6 = 4320.
Fixing Ava first leaves eight performers: 8! = 40320. Also fixing Noah last leaves seven performers: 7! = 5040.
Either category starts. Each alternating pattern permits 5! × 5! = 14400 orders, giving 2 × 14400 = 28800.
Even endings are 2 or 8, giving 2 × 6P3 = 2 × 120 = 240. Numbers greater than 7000 start with 7, 8 or 9, giving 3 × 6P3 = 360.
Arrange three subject blocks and independently order each block: 3! × 2! × 3! × 5! = 6 × 2 × 6 × 120 = 8640.

Six boys have 6! orders and create seven gaps. Injectively placing three distinct girls gives 7P3 = 210 choices, so 720 × 210 = 151200. The diagram shows six B labels and seven gap marks. Ordered gap placement equals the source's selection followed by internal arrangement.
All orders number 7! = 5040. Adjacent Mia and Leo form six units with two internal orders: 6! × 2! = 1440. Subtraction gives 3600.

Starting with 4 or 6 gives two first-digit choices and three available even endings: 2 × 3 × 5P2 = 120. Starting with 5 permits four even endings: 4 × 5P2 = 80. The disjoint cases total 200; zero is permitted only after the first position.

All seven people have 7! = 5040 orders. Adjacent teachers give 6! × 2! = 1440. Exactly one intervening student gives five student choices, five unit orders and two teacher orders: 5 × 5! × 2! = 1200. Subtracting both disjoint exclusions leaves 2400.

review.summary: All nine distinct assessed methods are correctly mapped and covered by source-supported examples within the target scope. All 25 exact assessment locators occur once. There are no existing examples to audit. Separate prompts and solutions, single-dollar mathematics, phantom gutters and renderer-inherited blue solution prose/math comply with the supplied requirements. The planar gaps diagram is consistent; actual rendering and final-size typography remain for the coordinator's visual stage. No syllabus exception is needed. Accepted practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited.

inspection.summary: Inspected all 36 desktop and mobile example and question-only images. Questions are black; solution prose and mathematics are blue, with invisible phantom gutters and aligned continuation relations. Content is readable and unclipped. Example 6 shows six readable black B labels and seven gap markers with correct relationships. All question-only views hide the working and solution diagram without revealing answers. No consequential visual defects found.
